source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], several components were absent from the 3D viewer when I opened the integrated board because some 3D models reference libraries available only on your machine. Could you send these three files to me?

USB4215-03-A.stp (from your Vucko.3dshapes) — for USB1
Q\_SOT-23.step (from the JLCPCB plugin library) — for Q3
TS-1088-AR02016.step (from the JLCPCB plugin library) — for S1

After receiving them, [CLIENT_NAME_001] place them in the project’s libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/ folder. Thanks!

execution.observed_behavior: Several integrated-board components were absent from the 3D viewer because their model files referenced libraries available only on the freelancer's machine.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Also, FYI: when I opened the integrated board on my Linux machine, I found several absolute Windows paths and references to libraries that exist locally on your machine but not mine, which caused most components to be absent from the 3D viewer. I fixed this on my side. There were 12 hard-coded Windows paths like D:/KiCAD Projekti/Upwork/[CLIENT_NAME_003] Cicak/Radni/IoT\_Environmental\_Monitoring\_Device\_All/libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/... — I changed them to ${KIPRJMOD}/libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/... so they are relative. Because the files themselves are under libs/, this works across machines.

Handling this myself is not a problem; I only wanted to make you aware of it.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Yes. Also, ${KICAD8\_3RD\_PARTY} is the path variable for KiCad 8, while KiCad 9 uses ${KICAD9\_3RD\_PARTY}. Therefore, even if the JLCPCB plugin is installed on a machine, those references would still fail in KiCad 9.

value_updates.kicad_version_compatibility: Packaged model references must not depend on KiCad-version-specific third-party path variables that fail when moving between KiCad 8 and KiCad 9.
